function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

The user says: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" They want to calculate something about hypothesis testing? They mention sample mean 98.2, sample std dev 1.4, sample size 40, null hypothesis mean 98.6. They ask to compute the standard deviation? Actually they say "零假設檢定的標準差" which might mean "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test"? That doesn't make sense. Maybe they want to compute the standard error or the t-statistic? The phrase "以得到人口平均值為98.6" means "to get the population mean of 98.6". So maybe they want to compute the p-value for a t-test with null mean 98.6. The question: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" Might be incorrectly phrased. They likely want to compute the standard error of the mean (SEM) and then compute the t-statistic and p-value. The tool provided calculates p-value for a t-test. So we can call the function with sample_mean=98.2, population_mean=98.6, sample_std_dev=1.4, sample_size=40. The function returns p-value. But the user asked for "標準差" maybe they want the standard error? The standard error = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). That would be 1.4 / sqrt(40) = 1.4 / 6.3249 = 0.2215 approx. But the question: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" Could be "calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test to get the population mean of 98.6." That is ambiguous.

Maybe they want to compute the standard error of the mean under the null hypothesis? Actually the standard error uses sample std dev. So it's 0.2215. Then compute t-statistic: (98.2 - 98.6) / 0.2215 = -0.4 / 0.2215 = -1.805. Then p-value two-tailed: around 0.075. Let's compute precisely: t = -1.805. df = 39. p-value two-tailed: 2 * P(T <= -1.805). Using t distribution table: For df=39, t=1.685 gives p=0.10; t=1.685? Actually for df=30, t=1.697 gives p=0.10. For df=40, t=1.684 gives p=0.10. For t=1.805, p ~ 0.08. So p ~ 0.07. So answer: standard error ~0.2215, t-statistic ~-1.805, p-value ~0.07. But the user didn't ask for t-statistic or p-value explicitly. They asked for "標準差" maybe they want the standard error. So we can provide that.
